metric.why: Distributed AI training is unusually intolerant of network degradation; a lossy fabric shows up as wasted GPU-hours before it shows up as an outage.
metric.metric: Network latency, packet loss, and bandwidth
metric.definition: Continuous measurement of round-trip latency, loss rate, and utilization on the facility's internal fabric and external transit.

reading.body:
Network latency and packet loss are an operational metric for AI data centers because distributed training turns network degradation into wasted GPU-hours before it becomes an outage.

The metric sits in the uptime and redundancy category alongside UPS battery health, generator runtime, and SLA uptime compliance. That grouping is the point. Power redundancy keeps a facility running, and network measurement keeps the expensive work inside it from being silently thrown away. A generator failure is visible. A lossy fabric is not, which is why it has to be measured continuously rather than monitored for alarms.

For AI specifically, the cost of a degraded fabric is paid in compute that was already bought and powered. The data here defines the measurement, round-trip latency, loss rate, and utilization on internal fabric and external transit, but it carries no thresholds, no observed values, and no history. It does not say what loss rate is tolerable, how measurement is instrumented, or how this facility compares to any other. It establishes that the metric exists and why it belongs in an uptime category, nothing about performance.
